blocks.text: 07-LPG / landing pages and funnels Goes here. A breakdown of a 4-step framework for building high-converting B2B and lead-gen landing pages. Covers optimizing the "above the fold" section, structuring benefit-driven sections, reducing friction in conversion events (e.g., contact forms), and strategically placing social proof. Not here. • Paid media campaign setup or top-of-funnel traffic generation -> 06-MEA • Automated email marketing flows -> 09-EML

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details specific, actionable UX and copywriting strategies for B2B and lead-gen landing pages, focusing on how to convert existing traffic into qualified leads through reduced friction and targeted messaging. modules: [LPG] topics: [landing pages, conversion rate optimization, lead generation, B2B marketing, above the fold, copywriting, visual hierarchy, social proof, contact forms, progressive disclosure] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. the ROI of landing pages / arguing that doubling conversion rate is vastly superior to doubling traffic, as it amplifies the ROI of all existing ad spend and outreach; optimizing the above the fold / highlighting that 100% of visitors see this section but 60% never scroll past it, necessitating a clear value proposition, benefit-driven headline, and stacked social proof; headline copywriting frameworks / utilizing the "so that" principle to drill down to the ultimate customer benefit (e.g., "Land emails in the inbox so that you can close more deals so that you can scale your business") and matching the headline to the awareness level of the traffic; stacking social proof / moving beyond a single review to feature multiple forms of credibility (e.g., G2 badges, total users, client logos, and quantified results) immediately visible without scrolling; visual hierarchy / using font size, weight, and contrasting colors to guide the user's eye from the main headline down to a prominent Call to Action (CTA) button; reducing fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUDs) / placing risk-reversal elements (e.g., "no credit card required" or guarantees) directly underneath the CTA button; reducing friction in conversion events / optimizing contact forms by combining fields (e.g., Full Name instead of First/Last), adding benefit-driven copy next to the form, and ensuring CTA buttons are repeated throughout the page; progressive disclosure / a psychological UX tactic where a user is initially asked for one simple piece of information (e.g., email), and only after submitting are they prompted for more complex data, reducing perceived friction; strategic social proof placement / embedding targeted testimonials throughout the page that explicitly back up specific value propositions or overcome known objections.

The "So That" Copywriting Principle: A method for finding the true customer benefit by repeatedly asking "so that..." after a feature statement until you hit the core desired outcome (e.g., more revenue, saved time).

Progressive Disclosure: A UX tactic used on lead forms where a user is initially presented with only one simple field (like an email address), and upon interacting, the rest of the form fields are revealed, minimizing the initial perceived cognitive load.

Stacking Social Proof: The strategy of placing multiple, distinct types of social proof (e.g., a 5-star rating badge plus client logos plus a quantified case study result) strictly "above the fold" to maximize instant credibility.

FUD Reduction Placement: The specific design tactic of placing text that reduces Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt (like "No Credit Card Required" or "Free Trial") directly underneath the primary CTA button.
Skip. The intro hook promoting the speaker's agency results, mentions of Microsoft Clarity session recordings without deep strategic context, and the outro teasing the next video.
Scope mix. 15% baseline (general definitions of landing pages and above the fold), 85% growth (advanced B2B copywriting frameworks, UX psychology, and lead-gen CRO tactics). Volume. ~400 words.
